Lab Session - Introduction to Power BI

Welcome to the first lab session of the module

_PBI-01 Welcome to PowerBI.docx

In this lesson, you will learn how to use a few tools in Power BI for creating reports.

Make sure you watch the video before you start the task. It will give you an introduction to the module and to Power BI.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us during the sessions.

We hope you enjoy the lesson.

TU PowerBI Team

1) Lab Introduction - Video 1

Before starting the first task, watch this short video.

I included a quick overview of the module and I showed the first steps to get started with Power BI.

Click here to watch the Lab Introduction Video

2) Workbook - Introductive task on Power BI

In this task, you will see how easy it is to create easy BI Reports [BI Dashboard] in Power BI!

(If you need to install Power BI on your home machine, check the Installation Guide under Module Resources)

If you are using a TU Lab machine, you can find Power BI through AppsAnywhere: https://appsanywhere.tees.ac.uk/

Your student university email has been registered for access to Power BI through AppsAnywhere. Inform your tutor if your email has not been registered, and we will contact IT Help to request activation for your Power BI license. Tutor Instructions: Email IT Help requesting Power BI activation for student: [insert student email].

[Lab: My 1st BI Dashbaord - Superstore]

Getting_Started_With_PowerBI.pdf




superstore_dataset_2011-2015.csv




For the last activity of today's session, you will also need the file below

[Lab: My 2nd BI Dashboard - Covid]

covid.csv




[Lab: My 2nd BI Dashboard - Covid - Axis Challenge]

Once you have completed the last activity on the COVID dataset, can you re-create the chart below? You can try to do this yourself and do feel free to consult the guide provided in the post lab section below.

The main challenge will be to display all the labels on the x-axis (from 1 to 18). Can you do that?







Extension Tasks

As a PowerBI Developer: The following key resources will help you quickly become a proficient Developer in Business Intelligence via Microsoft PowerBI. Go through them to find out more about Power BI

Microsoft PowerBI Tutorial Video from Beginning to Pro 1hr
Microsoft Guided Learning
Follow Microsoft courses of videos and articles that walk you through how to accomplish common tasks with Power BI.
Samples
Review examples of dashboards, reports, and desktop files, and see how some of our partners are putting Power BI to use.
Documentation
View in-depth articles for all of Power BI’s tools and features, from getting started to advanced

PBi Post Lab Self-Study Guide: PowerBI Tips n Tricks from your PowerBI Tutors

Congratulations on building your First BI Dashboard - Supe

Video-Introduction to the lab session:

Click here to watch the video

1) Check your Power BI account

Before starting today's tasks, please take a moment to sign in to Power BI.

Open Power BI and select Sign in in the top right corner.

If you see your name, you're already signed in, so you can get started with today's tasks.




If you're able to sign in without any errors, please move into the next task.

If you can't sign in, please fill in the form below and we will activate your account. 

Thank you

1) Workbook 1

3) Designing the final dashboard

Use the file you've been working on to design a dashboard. 

Identify at least 3 business questions and try to use the optimal chart to answer those questions.

Check the links below to get new ideas on how to present your dashboard:

15 Best Power BI Dashboards

Top 10 Power BI Dashboards

Don't forget to publish your final dashboard on Padlet!

Can you make the dashboards below? 

Any help with the Theme? Check this video:

4) ICA Work - Checkpoint

Have you selected the Dataset for your ICA yet? Have you started thinking about the business solution you are going to implement?

Please don't underestimate the time needed to find a suitable dataset and pre-process it. You should have the final dataset as soon as possible.

Use the rest of this lesson to find a dataset and start the pre-processing steps (e.g. removing missing values, renaming columns, creating relationships).

When you submit your assessment you are agreeing that the statements below are true.

I am aware of the University’s Regulations on Cheating and Plagiarism and confirm that the work I submit via this module is my own and does not contain any unacknowledged material from other sources.
Work submitted via this module has not been submitted in full or in part towards the assessment requirements of another module or course. 
Academic Misconduct - What is it?

To understand what academic misconduct is please read the following resources:

What is academic misconduct? - Academic misconduct - LibGuides at Teesside University

Academic Misconduct Regulations

The link below will help you understand the academic misconduct regulations. Please read the content before submitting your work:

Academic misconduct regulations 

What follows is only a brief summary of the University’s Academic Misconduct procedure and should be read in conjunction with the full regulations provided above.

You are strongly recommended to read those Regulations. They provide a detailed explanation of academic misconduct, the procedures which must be followed when an academic misconduct offence is suspected, and the possible penalties.

Academic misconduct is defined by the University as:

‘Any action by a student which gives (or which has the potential to give) an unfair advantage in an examination or assessment, or to assist someone to gain an unfair advantage, or any activity likely to undermine the integrity essential to scholarship and research.’

In order to avoid academic misconduct, the University is committed to continually educate its students on how to develop good academic practice and writing skills. The following support is available and it is recommended that you take advantage of this:

* Advice and guidance from your Students’ Union (or equivalent);

* The University’s Learning Hub, based in the University’s Student & Library Services;

* Facility for students and staff to use plagiarism e:detection software;

* Briefings on academic misconduct provided at student induction events and during relevant modules;

* You are entitled to be accompanied to the Meeting/Hearing arranged under the Regulations by one friend who may not act as a representative or attend in any legal capacity unless permitted to do so by the person conducting the proceedings. Your friend may be a representative from your Students’ Union (or equivalent).

The following tips may help you to avoid academic misconduct:

Do:

* Familiarise yourself with the regulations and penalties that can be incurred. For professional programmes, a single case of academic misconduct may result in you being discontinued from your course.

* Make sure that you know how to correctly acknowledge other people’s work or opinions, and get feedback from your Tutor on whether or not you are doing this correctly.

* Take care when making notes
